title: Rabbi David Tawil: Understanding the Amida- "Sim Shalom"

chapters.about: Halakhic rules for concluding a series of blessings

chapters.title: Placement of Sim Shalom
chapters.about: Why peace is requested in the section of gratitude

chapters.title: Concluding the Amidah
chapters.about: Yihyu le-ratson and the role of verbalized prayer

summary: Rabbi Tawil explores the themes of the Sim Shalom blessing, explaining its placement at the end of the Amidah as a request for peace that enables the full acknowledgment of Hashem. He discusses the halakhic practice of answering Amen to one's own blessing in the context of concluding a series of prayers and examines the significance of peace as a name of Hashem. The class also covers the concluding verse of the Amidah, Yihyu le-ratson, reflecting on the importance of verbalizing prayer while acknowledging that Hashem knows the unspoken meditations of the heart.
questions: Why do we answer Amen to our own blessing at the end of the Amidah?
Why is the request for peace placed in the final section of the Amidah rather than the middle?
Why is Shalom considered a name of Hashem?
Why do we verbalize our prayers if Hashem already knows our thoughts?
